summary: Frontend-only smoke of the new smooth-scroll + candle-countdown work on /demo-trade. Countdown, per-frame smoothness within a bar, 5m timeframe, drag-without-fight, follow-resume, default zoom all PASS. Two problems found: (1) CRITICAL — at each candle rollover the live-vert-line-top jumps by a full bar width (~21.8px, exactly barSpacing) in a single frame, i.e. the exact whole-bar rollover jump this fix was supposed to remove; (2) on mobile 390x844 and after mouse-wheel zoom on desktop, the smooth drift stops (0 distinct positions across ~3s) even though the countdown keeps ticking — auto-follow appears to disengage silently in those two situations.

ui_bugs.issue: At a 1m candle rollover the live-vert-line-top x jumps ~21.8px (== barSpacing 22) in a single animation frame. Captured deterministically: countdown '01:00' -> '00:59', left goes 1286.13px -> 1307.93px in one rAF tick (max intra-candle jump is only 0.24px, so the discontinuity is exactly at bar boundary). This is the 'no whole-bar jump at rollover' requirement failing. Likely cause: when the new bar opens, `frac` resets from ~1 to 0 but the anchor bar index isn't advanced in the same frame, so scrollToPosition snaps back by one bar.

ui_bugs.component: TradeChart smooth-drift on mobile / after wheel zoom
ui_bugs.issue: On viewport 390x844 on fresh load, live-vert-line-top style.left had 1 distinct value over 210 rAF frames (~3.5s) even though countdown was ticking (00:04, 00:01 seen). Same symptom after mouse-wheel zoom on desktop (1 distinct position over 2.5s). Countdown badge itself is fine — only the fractional scroll animation stalls. Probably the >2.5 bars follow-off guard is triggering because the initial fit / zoom leaves the range slightly past the live edge, so followRef stays false.

action_items: PRIMARY: fix the ~22px single-frame jump at candle rollover in the rAF drain in TradeChart.jsx. When the tick stream advances to a new bar, advance the scroll anchor by one bar in the same frame that `frac` resets to 0 (e.g. keep a runningPos = liveBarIndex + frac, or subtract 1 from frac for one frame after the boundary) so scrollToPosition(BASE_RIGHT_OFFSET + frac) doesn't rewind by a full bar. Repro: on /demo-trade wait until countdown hits 00:03, sample document.querySelector('[data-testid=live-vert-line-top]').style.left every rAF for 10s; the frame where cd goes 01:00->00:59 shows left 1286->1307.

SECONDARY: mobile fresh-load and post-wheel-zoom leave followRef=false. Either relax the 2.5-bar guard on those code paths, or explicitly re-arm follow after the initial fit and after a wheel event when the range's right edge is within a small tolerance of the live bar. Repro: 390x844 viewport, /demo-trade, no interaction — live-vert x stays constant for 3+ seconds while countdown keeps ticking.
After fixing #1, please retest drawings + indicators + a $1 DEMO UP trade across a rollover — they were deferred in this run.
critical_code_review_comments: The 'follow off if range >2.5 bars away' check is applied to too many code paths (initial mount, wheel zoom) — anywhere the range shifts slightly during layout the user ends up with a silently-frozen view. Consider anchoring the guard to actual user pointer input only.
The fractional scroll and the bar-index advance appear to be decoupled — the boundary transition needs to update both atomically in the same rAF or the jump is inevitable.

rca of the issue: In TradeChart.jsx rAF drain, ts.scrollToPosition(BASE_RIGHT_OFFSET + frac, false) is called every frame where frac ∈ [0,1) is the elapsed fraction of the CURRENT live bar. When a new bar opens, frac resets to ~0 but the price series' logical live-bar index has also advanced by +1 — so the effective x should stay continuous. It doesn't, which strongly suggests the code recomputes frac against the new bar without advancing whatever bar-index the scroll anchor is measured from within the same frame, producing a one-bar rewind (== barSpacing = 22px). Fix: track cumulative position (liveBarIndex + frac) or, on the frame that crosses the boundary, offset scrollToPosition by -1 so the visual x is preserved, then let subsequent frames continue with the fresh frac.
